newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end off highs after BHP slip.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end off highs after BHP slip.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2264 +11 US 30yr cl 7.07 -0.04
*Shares ended slightly firmer but well off highs after BHP slipped mid-morning *Total volume 301.4 million shares worth A$702.1 million, 974 stocks traded, 275 steady, 360 rises, 339 falls
The Australian share market closed slightly firmer on Tuesday but early gains were pared by bellwether BHP which dipped on comments by its managing director and profit downgrades by major brokers.
The key All Ordinaries index closed 5.1 points higher at 2,255.9, well off its intraday high of 2267.5.
The September share price index futures finished 11 points up at 2,264 and at a 8.1 point premium to the underlying index.
BHP managing director John Prescott told Reuters the steel market may be worsening and that the copper price remained a challenge for the world's second largest copper producer.

The share market's performance was disappointing, following Wall Street's surge on Monday, said dealer Diane Jenner of Sydney broker Dicksons. Jenner said Prescott's mid-morning comments about the domestic steel market and the international copper market helped drive the company's shares lower.
Prescott's negative comments followed a number of recent profit downgrades for BHP by Australian analysts.
Dealers said the outlook for Australian shares on Wednesday remained dependent on volatile U.S. markets but they said a Dow pullback after its two-day surge would not be overly negative.
Companies reporting on Tuesday included GIO Insurance which posted a flat full year net profit of A$142.2 million.
Its shares were slightly firmer early but weakened as the overall market eased from its highs.
Gaming machine manufacturer Aristocrat Leisure reported its maiden result as a listed company, posting a full year net profit of A$17.84 million.
Grocery wholesaler and retailer Davids said its year net profit rose to A$51.8 million from A$46.3 million.
Rises narrowly outnumbered falls on the day while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian bonds followed the U.S. bond market higher and ignored a jump in local housing finance data for July, the market seen held hostage by U.S. Treasuries until the release of local employment data on Thursday.
In late trade, the 10 year T-bond was yielding 8.09 percent, down 0.03 from Monday.
The Australian dollar held steady late in the session as the market settled into its new trading range around 80 cents.
By 5.10 p.m. (0710 GMT) the unit was quoted at US$0.8000/05
Dealers said business was again two-way with samurai-linked and U.S. fund buying balanced by Asian offers.
